ALPR technology has a way of drawing real community debate wherever it shows up, so this one is worth your attention. Tuesday, the **Telluride Town Council** meets with two items worth your attention: a work session on the Flock Safety automated license plate reader system, with Chief Marshal Josh Comte presenting — ALPR technology has a way of generating serious debate about privacy wherever it shows up — and a public hearing on extending the vesting period for property rights at 221 W Colorado, with that project's Certificate of Appropriateness expiring October 18. Up in Ouray County, the **Ouray County Board of County Commissioners Special Work Session** dedicates the day to the 2027 budget, with the Sheriff's Office getting dedicated time before the broader discussion. On the lighter side Tuesday evening, **CORAL SKYE** plays a live show on N Cora Street in Ridgway.
Wednesday is a heavy day for governance across the region. The **Mountain Village Town Council Meeting** runs all day as the annual budget work session — revenues, administration, the capital plan, economic development, Tourism Fund, Telluride Conference Center, gondola and chondola operations, community grants, parks and recreation — the full picture before formal adoption later in the year. The **San Miguel County Board of County Commissioners Meeting** also has a full agenda: two public hearings, including one on whether to waive land use application fees for Mountain Village's affordable housing project in the Ilium Valley, plus a 90-minute review of the 2027 preliminary budget. The **Telluride Housing Authority Subcommittee** meets to catch up on three months of draft minutes and consider a mortgage exception for a buyer under contract at 1001 E. The **Telluride Ecology Commission** holds its regular public meeting as well. On the lighter side, **A Monster Calls** screens Wednesday evening at **The Wright Opera House** in Ouray — a 2016 film about grief and imagination that hits harder than you'd expect.
Thursday, the **San Miguel County Planning Commission Meeting** opens with a joint work session with the **San Miguel County Board of County Commissioners** on an Affordable Housing Code Update — the county is still working to write policy fast enough to keep pace with the housing situation, and this is where that effort lives on paper. The **SMART Board of Directors** also meets Thursday; the agenda hadn't posted at press time. On the lighter side, **Shrek The Musical** from **Not-So-Young People's Theater** opens Thursday night at the Sheridan Opera House in Telluride, running through Sunday — local cast, original songs, and a ogre with a lot of heart.
Friday, the **Ridgway Farmer's Market** runs 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Hartwell Park — one of the last markets of the season before mid-October closes it out. Saturday, the **Ridgway Star Party** with the **Black Canyon Astronomical Society** starts at 7:30 p.m. at Ridgway Athletic Park ��� free, open to the public, professional telescopes and laser constellation tours, weather permitting. Sunday, the **Volunteer Trail Work Day: Cross Mountain Trailhead** wraps up the fall trail season — clearing debris, improving drainage, keeping the trails we all count on in good shape heading into winter.
